key_insight: Swarms of off-the-shelf AI coding agents, given only a scope statement and tool access, produced substantial research outputs in optimization and physical science, suggesting AI can already automate much routine theoretical research.
engineering_relevance: For computational science workflows, this points to agentic systems as scalable research assistants—but it also shifts the bottleneck from generation to verification, review, and governance.
method: Provided agents with a short scope description, literature access, and computing tools.
Ran the agents in an open-ended loop with one instruction: make real, correct, useful progress and do not stop.
Collected research notes, paper-length drafts, formal proofs, and proposed experiments across multiple domains.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the authors checked what they could, found no major scientific errors so far, and several results were formalized in a proof assistant, but a full review would take months.
watch_item: The main risk is verification overload: output can exceed human review capacity, so correctness, attribution, and publication standards may become difficult to enforce.
paper_title: AI Agent Swarms as Researchers: Progress, Challenges, and Open Questions
